brief.audience: Product, engineering, and functional leaders evaluating NodeSlide for production
brief.prompt: Create a 12-slide executive product and technical presentation about NodeSlide for research leaders, finance teams, startup founders, operators, governance committees, and the coding agents that support them. Communication job: prove that NodeSlide turns evidence and a brief into a defensible, editable, distributable decision artifact. Narrative: open on the gap between plausible AI output and a decision-ready deck; show the five production jobs and their distinct truth constraints; reveal the canonical deck-as-code architecture and one governed mutation path across UI, CLI, and MCP; explain source lineage, proposal-before-mutate, validation, receipts, editable PPTX/HTML/share exports, and agent operability; confront current failure modes honestly, especially brief drift, generic fallback copy, repetitive composition, and false green quality badges; then define the production acceptance gate and close with one owned rollout decision. Use one evolving visual metaphor: scattered signals become a structured story, cross a trust gate, then fan out as reusable institutional memory. The metaphor must visibly transform, not repeat as a progress rail. Use at least six materially different slide silhouettes, no adjacent repeated composition, no dashboard-card collage, no decorative metrics, no placeholder media, and no invented claims. Prefer diagrams, process grids, comparison, architecture, lineage, a truthful scorecard, and a decisive close over prose. Exactly 12 slides. Keep visible copy concise and make every slide advance the argument.
